questions.scenario: A clinic manager asks Claude to "explain the new booking system" in a message to the front-desk staff. The reply is correct, but it talks about API calls, time-slot objects and sync jobs, and the staff only use the booking screen. Which change to the prompt fixes this most directly?
questions.a: Add a limit: "Keep it under 100 words."
questions.b: Ask for the answer as a table, one row per change.
questions.c: Say who will read it: front-desk staff who book patients all day and don't know the system's technical terms.
questions.d: Paste the system's release notes into the prompt as background, in <context> tags.
questions.why: The weak answer came from a missing audience, and naming the readers sets the words, depth and tone.
questions.quote: It sets the words, the depth and the tone.
